ai_interpretation.executive_summary: On 2020-12-07, observed sessions increased by 42.0% relative to the 4-week baseline (5,461 vs. 3,846 sessions), while the purchase rate decreased relatively by 14.5% (from a baseline of 1.95% to 1.67%, representing a 0.28 percentage point decline). This rate contraction corresponds to an estimated shortfall of 15.5 purchase sessions relative to baseline rate expectations, while overall session volume expanded substantially.
ai_interpretation.why_no_alert: An anomaly alert was not triggered because the alert rule requires all three threshold criteria to be satisfied simultaneously. Although the session volume exceeded the 150-session threshold and the estimated purchase session gap of 15.5 cleared the minimum shortfall requirement of 15, the relative purchase rate drop of -14.5% did not meet the required minimum relative rate drop threshold of 35%. Consequently, the status remains classified as no_qualifying_anomaly.

hypotheses.title: Top-of-funnel promotional traffic dilution
hypotheses.explanation: A promotional campaign or external marketing push on 2020-12-07 may have introduced a surge of low-intent or exploratory visitors, increasing overall session volume by 42.0% while lowering the aggregate purchase session rate without an actual drop in baseline shopper intent.
data_needed: Session volume broken down by acquisition source, medium, and campaign for the target date and baseline dates
Landing page session distribution across the evaluated dates
Purchase rate segmented by campaign and traffic source
hypotheses.validation_check: Compare channel- and campaign-level traffic growth rates against their respective purchase rate trends to determine if traffic increases were concentrated in channels exhibiting lower historical conversion rates.

hypotheses.title: Device or technical checkout friction
hypotheses.explanation: Technical or usability defects introduced on specific device types or browser platforms could have impaired users' ability to reach purchase confirmation, dampening the purchase rate despite elevated traffic.
data_needed: Device category, operating system, and browser platform session distributions
Purchase rates segmented by device and browser platform
Technical error or exception tracking logs corresponding to the date
hypotheses.validation_check: Evaluate platform-specific purchase rates to see if the decline is isolated to a specific device or browser cohort rather than distributed uniformly across all users.

hypotheses.title: Inventory stockouts or product availability constraints
hypotheses.explanation: The 42.0% traffic influx may have led to product stockouts, shipping lead time disclaimers, or unfulfilled merchandise intent, causing prospective purchasers to exit prior to completing a purchase.
data_needed: Product view and product detail page interaction counts
Cart addition metrics alongside inventory status records for highly trafficked items
Session-level progression between product view and purchase events
hypotheses.validation_check: Assess session progression between item detail views, cart actions, and purchases to determine whether drops occurred downstream of product views.

recommended_checks.purpose: Identify which traffic sources drove the 42.0% increase in sessions and whether the rate drop was concentrated within specific incoming cohorts.
inputs_needed: Sessions by source, medium, and campaign for 2020-12-07
Baseline sessions and purchase rates across matching acquisition dimensions

recommended_checks.purpose: Determine whether the 14.5% relative drop in purchase rate was systemic or isolated to a specific operating system, browser, or device type.
inputs_needed: Device category, browser, and operating system metrics for 2020-12-07 and baseline dates
Purchasing sessions grouped by platform attributes

recommended_checks.purpose: Determine at which stage of the shopping flow users exited to distinguish intent shifts from mid-funnel friction.
inputs_needed: Session-level event sequences including view_item, add_to_cart, begin_checkout, and purchase

limitations: No statistical significance tests were performed, so it cannot be confirmed whether the observed rate decline deviates beyond expected random variance.
Data is aggregated across all channels, masking potential channel-specific, device-specific, or geographic divergences.
Purchasing sessions indicate sessions with purchase activity and cannot be treated as order counts, units, or revenue metrics.
The 15.5 purchase session gap is a mathematical estimate based on baseline conversion rates and cannot be interpreted as confirmed lost sales.
True funnel progression and drop-off identification cannot be verified without session-level behavioural paths.
